title: Alvarez: sufficient for faith, efficacious for its preparations
source_text: XXXII. Id inter alios docet expresse Didacus Alvarez numero tertio capitis jam citati. Omne, inquit, auxilium sufficiens, comparatione unius actus, semper est efficax respectu alterius, ad quem efficiendum decreto absoluto divinae voluntatis destinatur. Ut, verbi gratia, auxilium sufficiens ad actum fidei, efficaciter producit in homine pias cogitationes, & notitias credendorum, vel pia desideria habendi fidem, & alios hujusmodi actus imperfectos, qui regulariter loquendo antecedunt assensum fidei. Similiter auxilium sufficiens ad actum contritionis producit efficaciter in homine considerationem poenarum inferni, vel attritionem, aut alios hujusmodi actus imperfectos qui regulariter perfectam contritionem antecedunt.
pass_a_gloss: XXXII. This among others teaches expressly Didacus Alvarez in number third of the chapter already cited. Every, he says, sufficient help, in comparison with one act, is always efficacious with respect to another, for effecting which it is destined by an absolute decree of the divine will. As, for example, sufficient help for the act of faith, efficaciously produces in man pious thoughts, and knowledge of things to be believed, or pious desires of having faith, and other imperfect acts of this kind, which regularly speaking precede the assent of faith. Similarly sufficient help for the act of contrition produces efficaciously in man the consideration of the pains of hell, or attrition, or other imperfect acts of this kind which regularly precede perfect contrition.
pass_b_english: Thesis XXXII. Diego Alvarez, among others, teaches this expressly in section 3 of the chapter already cited: 'Every aid that is sufficient with respect to one act is always efficacious with respect to another, which an absolute decree of the divine will has appointed it to bring about.

'For example, aid sufficient for the act of faith effectively produces in a person devout thoughts and knowledge of what is to be believed, or devout desires to have faith, and other incomplete acts of this kind which, as a rule, come before the assent of faith. Likewise aid sufficient for the act of contrition effectively produces in a person reflection on the pains of hell, or attrition, or other incomplete acts of this kind which as a rule come before perfect contrition.'

knowledge of things to be believed

choices.why: Sorrow for sin from fear of punishment versus sorrow from love of God; the standard terms kept.
